questions.question: OP-01/O73 (readinto1): D126 says readinto1(b) writes 1 to min(len(b), r) bytes 'in at most one backend request', the rule D78 withdrew for read1 (retries and resumes apply as to read; request count is NP2's). A reset inside readinto1, resumed per D39/D72, is the second request D126 forbids. Which wording?

options.label: As read1, per D78 (Recommended)
options.description: readinto1(b) writes 1 to min(len(b), r) bytes as soon as at least one is available, without waiting to fill b, 0 at the end; retries and resumes as read (D38, D39), request count NP2's. Source: D78, io.BufferedIOBase.readinto1. One rule for both one-shot reads.

options.label: Keep one-request rule
options.description: readinto1 alone makes at most one backend request: no retry or resume inside it, so a reset surfaces at once and moves the stream to Failed. Diverges from read1 (D78) and makes request count a promise against NP2.

cd
ef

options.label: io's: exceeds (Recommended)
options.description: readlines(hint) with hint > 0 stops after the line that makes the total exceed hint; hint <= 0 reads to the end. Matches io.IOBase.readlines, which D70 and D126 adopt. Source: io.IOBase.readlines (✓ run in O73).

options.label: Keep 'reaches'
options.description: Stops once the total reaches hint: readlines(3) above returns [b'ab\n']. A library-specific rule that code written against io would see differ by one line.

questions.question: OP-01/O74 (NP9 scope): readlines(hint) returns whole readline() results, so readlines(10) over 1,000,000 bytes with no newline returns one 1,000,000-byte line (run in the review); yet D133 says D40's memory bound covers readlines with a positive hint. How is that resolved?

options.label: NP9 takes readlines (Recommended)
options.description: NP9's scope reads: readline with a negative limit, readlines at any hint, and line iteration, both forms (D40, D71, D126); D133's restatement and D126's NP9 sentence amended alike. io semantics kept; the bounded way to read lines stays readline(limit). Source: io.IOBase.readlines, D71.

options.label: Hint bounds each line
options.description: readlines(hint) reads each line with a limit, so a line longer than the bound is split into several list elements: D40's bound holds, but readlines then differs from io and from repeated readline() (D126, D70).

OP-01/O76 (cancelled close, sync SDK): D118 says a cancelled close() leaves the stream Closed with every local resource released, the connection aborted. On a backend whose async form runs the SDK's close in a worker thread (SFTP via paramiko, per the review), cancelling asyncio.to_thread propagates the cancellation while the thread runs on: the release completes after the caller is told (run in the review). What holds there?

options.label: Declare a deviation (Recommended)
options.description: D118 stays the normal value. Deviation, declared by a backend whose async close runs in a worker thread (SFTP): the stream is Closed when the cancellation propagates, a later close() a no-op, the release completes when the worker's close returns, never left to garbage collection. D43 gains a seventh point, Cancelled close; O13 reads seven. Source: D43's reason (weaker side), asyncio.to_thread (✓ run in O76).

options.label: Shield, then propagate
options.description: Such a backend's cancelled close waits for its worker's close to return, then propagates the cancellation: D118 holds everywhere, no new variation point, but the cancellation arrives late by the close's duration (D12's bounds on the network side, D14's deviation for the server's disk).

options.label: Abort from the loop
options.description: D118 holds as written: the async form aborts the connection by closing the SDK's socket from the event loop's thread. Not run; reaches into the SDK's internals (paramiko's own transport thread), which no ground or prior art here vouches for.
